subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary web_fetch URLs, and if so should the supported API be nested or per-agent ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork rather than the requested top-level allowPrivateNetwork key?
rationale: The low-level guard can already bypass private-network checks, but exposing that as public config changes the SSRF security boundary and overlaps an open draft implementation whose API, threat model, and proof still need maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt nested/per-agent audited policy
options.body: Proceed with a default-off ssrfPolicy-style API, explicit dangerous naming, audit/docs, and upgrade/security proof before closing the issue.

options.title: Use a global broad opt-in
options.body: Expose a simpler global default-off private-network switch, accepting less per-agent isolation in exchange for a smaller configuration surface.

options.title: Reject broad private-network access
options.body: Keep arbitrary web_fetch URLs strict and limit supported exceptions to existing narrow fake-IP flags, proxies, or future allowlist-only designs.

recommendation.title: Adopt nested/per-agent audited policy
recommendation.body: Proceed with a default-off ssrfPolicy-style API, explicit dangerous naming, audit/docs, and upgrade/security proof before closing the issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the clearest prior policy review on the related private-network PR shape and has recent SSRF/web-tools hardening history.
